title: Comparative evaluation of LLM-only, LLM+RAG, and LLM+RAG+Formal-Verifier pipelines for preventing actionable NetOps misconfigurations (repaired preregistration)
research_question: How much do RAG augmentation and a downstream formal network verifier reduce the rate of actionable misconfigurations produced by LLM-generated network-change proposals on realistic public topologies and incident-change tasks, and what are the operational trade-offs (end-to-end latency, verifier failure rates)?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: An LLM+RAG pipeline (Treatment B) produces a lower actionable-misconfiguration rate than LLM-only (Baseline A) on the same paired task set (primary confirmatory hypothesis).

H2: Adding a formal network verifier to LLM+RAG (Treatment C) further reduces actionable-misconfiguration rate compared with LLM+RAG alone, at the cost of increased end-to-end latency (secondary confirmatory hypothesis).

H3: A majority of residual verified failures after the verifier stage are attributable to semantic policy-specification gaps rather than purely syntactic generation errors (exploratory confirmatory sub-hypothesis to be tested descriptively and by logistic regression).
exploratory_questions: EQ1: Which failure-mode taxons (missing ACL, wrong next-hop, route withdrawal, loop introduction, interface shutdown) dominate residual actionable failures per pipeline?
EQ2: How do retriever match scores and retrieval-document provenance correlate with residual failures?
benchmark_scope: Public topology task set assembled from public topology collections (see sampling_plan) and incident-derived change intents; scope explicitly limited to those public/synthesized topologies and emulated vendor CLIs.
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API endpoint (identifier: hosted-llm-api-1) used for all generation calls to avoid multi-model generality claims; embedding/embedding-api-1 used for retrieval embedding. All calls use the hosted model API available per capability_manifest.
transformation_scope: RAG retrieval (embeddings + vector index), LLM generation prompts (fixed templates), deterministic parser-based configuration normalization, Batfish-style formal verification (containerized Batfish vX image), and simulator-based service-impact emulation using containerized vendor-CLI emulators.
primary_estimand: Paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate between LLM+RAG (B, guarded) and LLM-only (A, baseline) across the same tasks (estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline as required by available_analysis_contracts.paired_binary_analysis_v1).
secondary_estimands: Paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate between LLM+RAG+Verifier (C) and LLM+RAG (B).
Median and IQR of end-to-end latency per pipeline (paired comparisons).
Verifier precision and recall computed against simulator-detected outages (simulator treated as reference for detectable outages).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired sample of N=200 distinct change-intent tasks. Each task is executed under three deterministic treatments on the same frozen intent text: (A) LLM-only, (B) LLM+RAG, (C) LLM+RAG+Verifier. Inclusion: tasks drawn from public incident descriptions and synthetic variants (see public sources below) that (a) are expressible as a single atomic change intent and (b) are executable on emulated vendor-CLI topologies included in the public topology set. Exclusion: tasks requiring non-public data or human operator credentials. Public topology and emulator choices (images, versions) will be published with checksums in the experiment artifacts: Internet Topology Zoo subset (hashes published) and synthetic spine-leaf topologies derived from publicly available container network images; vendor-CLI emulation via containerized open-source CLI emulators (Batfish-compatible CLI images and a documented Cisco-like IOS emulator image; exact image tags and SHA256 hashes will be recorded in the execution manifest). Confirmatory items = 200 (paired tasks). Discovery items = 0 (all confirmatory).
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory analysis uses the supplied paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor (estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). For each task produce binary actionable-misconfiguration flags for each treatment using deterministic rules (see contamination_plan). Primary test: McNemar-style paired binary test implemented by paired_binary_analysis_v1 producing absolute difference, odds ratio, and 95% CI. Report two-sided p-values and Clopper–Pearson intervals for per-treatment rates. Secondary: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test on latency distributions. Verifier precision/recall: compare verifier pass/fail to simulator-detected service-impact (simulator as reference) with Clopper–Pearson intervals. Correct for multiplicity of main confirmatory contrasts (B vs A primary; C vs B secondary) using Benjamini–Hochberg on the two confirmatory p-values. Preplanned sensitivity analyses: (1) treat failed or unavailable model calls as automatic failures (binary=1) and rerun analysis (complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity), (2) alternate actionable definition conservative (require both simulator outage AND verifier fail) and report as robustness check. All analyses executed by registered executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 (compatible_execution_adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1).
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory contrast pre-registered as B (LLM+RAG) vs A (LLM-only). Secondary confirmatory contrast C vs B. Apply Benjamini–Hochberg correction across these two confirmatory contrasts. All further contrasts are exploratory and reported as such.
missingness_plan: Model/API call failures and infrastructure faults are logged automatically. For a task-treatment pair where a technical failure prevents observing model output, the pair is included in the primary analysis under two prespecified treatments: (a) primary analysis excludes only tasks where the baseline A or B output is missing for both arms of a contrast (paired executor rule 'complete_pair_primary'); (b) sensitivity analysis treats technical-failure pairs as actionable failures (complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity). No human imputation or manual adjudication is used.

benchmark_names: Public topology set (ITZ-subset + synthetic spine-leaf subset)
risk_factors: Retrieval-corpus poisoning or low-provenance documents causing RAG misguidance
Simulator/verifier modeling mismatch with emulated vendor-CLI semantics
Nondeterministic LLM outputs and API rate-limit induced variability
detection_procedures: Provenance-check: every retrieved document must carry a documented source URL and checksum; retrievals lacking provenance are automatically excluded from the RAG context.

Cross-document consistency check: if top-3 retrieved documents provide mutually contradictory configuration templates (>2 distinct canonical syntaxes for same intent), flag retrieval as low-confidence and run an alternate prompt that omits retrievals for sensitivity analysis.
Retriever score threshold gating: retrievals with embedding similarity below a prespecified seedable threshold (0.65 cosine) are excluded automatically.
item_flagging_rules: If provenance is missing => exclude doc from RAG context (automatic exclusion).
If cross-document contradiction score > predefined threshold => mark task retrieval as 'low-confidence' and record for subgroup analysis (deterministic flag).
If verifier and simulator disagree (verifier pass but simulator outage) => label as 'verifier_simulator_disagreement' for automated downstream sensitivity analysis; do not perform human adjudication.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis labels actionable-misconfiguration = 1 if (simulator-detected service-impact == yes) OR (verifier reports property violation). For verifier/simulator disagreements the automated rule above determines labeling and the disagreement category is reported and analyzed as a planned subgroup. Sensitivity analyses include the conservative alternative requiring both verifier AND simulator to signal a fault.
residual_uncertainty: Residual construct-validity uncertainty from simulator fidelity vs production networks (recorded and reported as noncritical).
Residual uncertainty about adversarially poisoned public documents that evade provenance checks (reported as noncritical and discussed in limitations).

budget_scenarios.description: Full confirmatory run: N=200 paired tasks, single hosted LLM model (hosted-llm-api-1), one retriever/embedding configuration, Batfish-style verifier container. Conservative repair-loop budget allowing up to 2 automated repair prompts per task when verifier fails (average observed repairs per failing task estimated = 2).
models: hosted-llm-api-1 (generation, temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, deterministic decoding where supported)
transformations: Prompt templates v1 (frozen), retriever top-k=5 (seeded), vector index (FAISS-like, deterministic build), Batfish-container-v1 verification run
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Model-call arithmetic: per task calls = A:1 (LLM-only) + B:1 (LLM+RAG) + C:1 (initial LLM generation for LLM+RAG+Verifier) + C_repairs_avg:2 = 5 LLM calls per task. 5 calls/task * 200 tasks = 1,000 planned_model_calls. Verifier and simulator run locally in containers (docker_available=true) and do not consume hosted model calls. This fits capability_manifest maximum_planned_model_calls=10000 and can complete within the run-time budget.

budget_scenarios.description: Reduced confirmatory run for constrained budget: N=100 paired tasks; same architecture but no allowed repair-loop (repair attempts disabled; verifier-only blocking).
transformations: Prompt templates v1, retriever top-k=5 (seeded), Batfish-container-v1 verification run
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Model-call arithmetic: per task calls = A:1 + B:1 + C:1 = 3 calls/task. 3 calls/task * 100 tasks = 300 planned_model_calls. Lower cost but removes repair-loop measurements and reduces power for small effects.

power_plan.target_effect: Detect an absolute reduction in actionable-misconfiguration rate of 6 percentage points (e.g., 15% -> 9%) between A and B with two-sided alpha=0.05 and 80% power under approximate binomial paired assumptions.
power_plan.clustering_unit: individual task (paired within-task comparisons across treatments)
power_plan.calculation_method: Analytic approximation for paired binary comparisons (McNemar/paired_binary_analysis_v1) and simulation-based sensitivity checks; power calculation assumes independence across tasks and baseline misconfiguration prevalence ~0.15.
assumptions: Baseline actionable-misconfiguration rate for LLM-only (A) ≈ 15% (plausible given literature on domain hallucination; conservative default).
Paired correlation of binary outcomes moderate (unknown); power approximations use worst-case conservative assumptions.
No more than 5% technical-failure pairs (handled by sensitivity analyses).
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=200 paired tasks and baseline 15%, the study can detect ~6 percentage-point absolute reductions with ~80% power under the stated assumptions; if baseline is lower (<10%) detectable absolute effect grows larger. These are approximations; exact power numbers will be produced by paired_binary_analysis_v1 pre-execution power routine and recorded in the execution manifest.
sensitivity_analyses: Repeat power estimates under baseline rates 10% and 20% and under varying paired outcome correlations (0.1–0.5).
Assess power when treating technical failures as failures (conservative).

transformation_families: Simulator run (containerized CLI replay) → service-impact detection
semantic_equivalence_checks: Automated parser checks: normalize generated CLI to canonical internal representation and verify that the set of intended ACL/prefix modifications appear in the normalized output (deterministic string/AST comparisons).

Round-trip check: reingest normalized config into the simulator and verify that key caller-specified observable properties (reachability between named endpoints in intent) are not inverted relative to baseline when verifier reports pass.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject generated outputs if parsing fails deterministically (syntax errors) — automatically log as syntactic-failure.
Reject and mark for repair-loop if verifier reports property violation — automatic repair prompt generated with deterministic template (no human adjudication).
Reject retrievals lacking provenance or below similarity threshold (automatic exclusion).
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Audit sample: deterministic 10% random seed-based sample of generated outputs and verifier/simulator outcomes will be exported as reproducibility bundle (hashed) for external inspection. Audit is automatic (no human annotation) and serves reproducibility trace; sampling seed recorded in manifest.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Vendor-CLI mapping validated by automated unit tests in containers: for each vendor image used, deterministic test fixtures exercise a representative set of commands and expected parser outputs; fixtures and their hashes published in artifacts.
residual_risks: Parser or mapping bugs that mis-interpret vendor CLI constructs (documented and included in residual_uncertainty).
Verifier modeling gaps for semantic policies not expressible in verifier property language.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Simulator/digital-twin fidelity relative to production networks (construct validity) — acknowledged and bounded to public/emulated topologies.
Degree to which retriever/corpus quality vs RAG design drive observed benefits (possible confounding; planned subgroup analyses and sensitivity across retriever thresholds).
Formal verifier false negatives for semantic policies not expressible in verifier language (will be reported and analyzed descriptively).
Adversarial retrieval-poisoning residual risk beyond provenance exclusion rules (discussed as limitation).
Detectable minimum effect depends on true baseline prevalence and paired correlation (power approximations provided; exact numbers recorded pre-execution).
